newsitem.title: UK: Britain vows to block common EU immigration policy.
newsitem.headline: Britain vows to block common EU immigration policy.

text.p: Britain bluntly told its European Union partners on Thursday that it wanted nothing to do with proposals for a common immigration policy and centralised controls over the EU's borders.

Plans to bring aspects of home and justice affairs under the umbrella of EU institutions, as part of a revision of the 1991 Maastricht treaty, will be discussed by EU leaders at a summit in Dublin next week.

"We can't stop discussion, but our position is entirely clear and has been for a very long time -- we have no intention of doing anything whatever which will weaken our frontier controls," Home Secretary Michael Howard told BBC radio.
Howard, the interior minister, said Britain would not hesitate to use its veto.
"It's quite simple, it's quite straightforward. There's no doubt about it whatever...
"If it's necessary in order to defend Britain's interests, we will be isolated in Europe. We would rather defend Britain's interests than foresake that isolation," Howard said.

Prime Minister John Major, who won opt-outs at Maastricht from monetary union and a social chapter covering workers' rights, is under intense pressure from right-wing members of his ruling Conservative Party to step aside from further integration in Europe.

The main opposition Labour party, favourite to win a general election now no more than five months away, also opposes significant extensions of the EU's competences and says it would retain Britain's veto in immigration matters.
